name: Yaoundé
subtitle: Yaoundé, capital of Cameroon: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,881,876 people lived across Yaoundé's seven arrondissements in the 2005 census (projected over 3.7 million today).
Known as the 'City of Seven Hills', Yaoundé was founded in 1889 as a German interior post before becoming the French mandate capital.
The Reunification Monument and the National Museum preserve the political and cultural memory of Cameroon's unique post-colonial union.

parts.text: Yaoundé was established in February 1889 by German explorer Richard Kund as a colonial research and military base among the Ewondo communities, strategically positioned across a scenic landscape of lush rolling hills.
Following the First World War and the partition of German Kamerun, Yaoundé was selected by French colonial authorities as their administrative capital in 1921, succeeding Douala on the coast.
Upon national independence in 1960 and the subsequent reunification with British Southern Cameroons in 1961, Yaoundé became the permanent sovereign capital of the Republic of Cameroon.

blocks.prompt: About how many people were counted in Yaoundé in the 2005 census?

parts.text: 1,881,876 in the 2005 3rd General Population Census across Yaoundé's seven arrondissements. Recent national demographic projections place the metropolitan population above 3.7 million.

items.text: German expedition under Richard Kund establishes an interior outpost at Yaoundé.
French authorities designate Yaoundé the capital of French Cameroon, shifting power from Douala.
Cameroon achieves independence, establishing Yaoundé as the national capital.
The Reunification Monument is completed on Plateau Atemengue.
The Basilica of Mary Queen of the Apostles at Mvolyé is consecrated.
